newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate moderates early gains - SEPT 25.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate moderates early gains - SEPT 25.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates reined in earlier gains to close just 15 basis points up at 22.25 percent at greater volume and after a more calm session than on many recent days, traders said.
"Far quieter and much greater volume than in other sessions. The pace speeded up without affecting the forex market," a trader said.
Traders said that volume increased as trade had picked up in term instruments.

"Term rates were moving above and below the new primary rates, which shows the market is lining up with the new primary curve. Those who needed paper stepped into buy, and those who wanted to take profits stepped in to sell towards the close," the trader added.
Secondary 91-day and 182-day Cetes rates closed at 26.94 percent and 28.25 percent, respectively, or slightly above new primary rates at 26.75 percent and 28.16 percent.
Overnight bank paper meanwhile closed 50 basis points up at 24.70 percent.
Liquidity pressures on Thursday were expected to arise from credit maturities totaling 2.002 billion pesos and an oversupply of 991 million pesos from the primary auction.
